text_blocks.snippet: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) diagnosis involves confirming that breast cancer cells lack receptors for estrogen, progesterone, and HER2. This is determined through immunohistochemistry and other tests on biopsied tissue. TNBC is considered more aggressive than other breast cancer types and is often diagnosed in younger women and those of African American descent.
